items.description: $1.2 million was paid out at Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 for exploits targeting phones, printers, smart speakers, smart home hubs, and AI infrastructure and coding tools. The post Google Pixel 10 Exploits Earned Hackers $560,000 at Pwn2Own appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.description: The Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 hacking contest has concluded, with hackers collecting $1,262,000 in rewards after exploiting 98 zero-day flaws. [...]

items.title: Formula Predicts When AI Chatbots Are at Risk of Turning Bad
items.description: Researchers from George Washington University have published a paper examining whether the time and cause of AI going rogue can be predicted. The post Formula Predicts When AI Chatbots Are at Risk of Turning Bad appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: FBI disrupts Chinese hacking tools used to breach critical infrastructure
items.description: The FBI has seized seven domains used by Chinese state-sponsored hackers known as Flax Typhoon to operate two hacking tools, MicroScan and FishHub, used in attacks that breached critical infrastructure and other organizations worldwide. [...]

items.title: 'AgentCorruption' Puts AWS Environments At Risk With Single Prompt
items.description: A now-patched vulnerability in AWS Bedrock AgentCore could allow an attacker to use one AI chatbot to take over an organization's entire fleet.

items.title: Ransomware attack disrupts Japan's IDCF Cloud used by govt clients
items.description: IDC Frontier, a major Japanese cloud and digital infrastructure company, disclosed that its IDCF Cloud service was targeted in a ransomware attack that caused an outage at a data center cluster serving the eastern part of the country. [...]

items.title: Low-cost Android phones ship with residential proxy malware
items.description: A malware campaign dubbed 'Midnight Mimosa' has been discovered on low-cost Android smartphones that ship with malicious software embedded in their firmware, allowing attackers to silently install apps, perform ad fraud, and turn devices into residential proxies. [...]

items.title: Venezuelan Cartel's Malware Honcho Nabbed for ATM Jackpotting
items.description: The first cybercriminal to ever make the FBI's "10 Most Wanted Fugitives" list allegedly infused Tren de Aragua's violent criminal operations with cash.

items.title: FakeGit malware campaign returns with 17,610 malicious GitHub repos
items.description: More than 17,000 fake repositories on GitHub are distributing the SmartLoader malware after the FakeGit campaign reactivated earlier this month to push the StealC infostealer. [...]

items.title: Japan Sees Sharp Rise in Web Data Leaks Amid Mobile API Abuse and Metabase Attacks
items.description: Attackers behind a string of personal data leaks at Japanese organizations have abused APIs for mobile apps and targeted known software flaws, the JPCERT Coordination Center (JPCERT/CC) said. According to TrendAI, the malware has been put to use in attacks targeting Ukrainian government personnel. items.description: All enterprises conduct security awareness training for their employees. But whether this has tangible benefits is debatable. The post Security Awareness Training Isn’t Dead, but It Needs a Rethink appeared first on SecurityWeek.
